technical_validation.duplicate_guard_evidence: r4.checkpoint and r4.rebuild_manifest reject duplicate case/target ownership with checkpoint_duplicate_target; current registry read found one owner per target.
technical_validation.qualification: Mutable global registry was read only for ownership and deliberately not hash-locked.

items.evidence: Paragraph 97 states that the duty of fairness varies depending on context.
items.scope_review: The contextual limit is exact. The separate Baker-factor list is not duplicated into this AU.

items.evidence: Paragraph 116 calls the failure to submit the June 10 final investigation report containing analysis and findings for applicant comment before final approval a fundamental problem and later a fatal flaw.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this is not a duty to circulate every investigative document. The exact report/date/pre-approval limits and paragraphs 173-174 witness are indispensable and present.

items.evidence: Paragraph 97 lists the five contextual Baker considerations after the court says consideration must first be given to them.
items.scope_review: Qualification: the list-only primary span does not independently establish speaker/adoption. The preceding court introduction is therefore mandatory attribution context and is recorded as an exact cross-block attribution witness. The factors are not five unconditional duties.

items.evidence: Paragraph 25 combines non-party history, an express assumption that the employer was not represented, and a hypothetical conflict if it were represented by the respondent.
items.scope_review: The passage does not find actual concurrent representation or adjudicate a conflict. A fact-only negative is plausible, but unresolved is safer because the court makes a conditional legal inference whose AU kind and reusable scope remain uncertain.

items.evidence: Paragraph 84 paraphrases paragraph 69(a): for fraud, the Commission may revoke or not make an appointment as applicable.
items.scope_review: Fraud condition and as-case-may-be limit are exact. The unanswered third-party corrective-action question and later jurisdiction reservation are not converted into a holding.

items.evidence: Paragraph 96 expressly applies correctness to the alleged procedural-fairness breach.
items.scope_review: The exact fairness limit prevents misuse as a jurisdiction/reasonableness standard; no suppressed authority is invented.

items.evidence: Paragraph 181 is a rhetorical reflection on judicial dialogue, truth-telling and argument quality.
items.scope_review: It contains no operative remedy, costs entitlement or reusable test.

items.evidence: Paragraph 190 awards increased costs above ordinary Column III costs and identifies the factors determining discretion.
items.scope_review: Exceptional-case condition, ordinary-default qualification, case and costs limits are all explicit. It does not award automatic solicitor-and-client costs or adopt either party's requested amount.

items.evidence: Paragraph 48 reproduces English section 69 with separate suspicion and satisfaction thresholds and permissive investigation/remedy powers.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this is statutory text, not a current-court holding that independent corrective action against this third party was lawful. The two thresholds, permissive `may`, remedy limits and later jurisdiction reservation must remain intact; the proposal preserves them.

items.evidence: Paragraph 165 appraises incompleteness concerning the applicant's actual tasks and supervisory functions.
items.scope_review: It states no universal manager-interview duty or freestanding investigation test.

boundaries.note: This report independently accepts only the frozen sixth10 model-silver decisions; mutable overall R4 progress remains outside scope.
